journey.description: Faith rarely develops in a straight line. We inherit beliefs, encounter questions, search, rebuild, embody, and awaken—often revisiting each season with greater honesty and depth. Questions do not have to weaken faith; they can lead us toward a faith that is more resilient, alive, and truly our own.

circles.description: Homeward Circles are eight-week guided experiences for 6–8 people who want deeper faith, real friendship, and room for honest questions. No expertise, polished answers, or prior meditation experience is required.

founder.heading: A fellow traveler.
paragraphs: I studied religion in college and have spent about thirty years in retreats, meditation, and contemplative practice. Along the way I also ran and grew a successful multi-site manufacturing business — but the thing I longed for most, I kept not finding.

In church after church I found beautiful worship and often a genuinely good message. What was missing was the deeper part: the transformative practices that have formed people for centuries, and honest space to bring doubt, ask hard questions, and wrestle with faith out loud. That wrestling is how faith becomes your own — how we come to know God, and ourselves, more deeply.
Homeward is the community I was looking for. I'd love to find the people who've been looking for it too.
founder.disclaimer: Homeward isn't meant to be about one person. I'm simply leading at the start so trust can form and other voices can emerge.

rooted_line: Rooted in the life and way of Jesus, Homeward is open to all who genuinely seek God in love. We welcome faith, questions, hope, doubt, and uncertainty.

items: Remembering that we do not have to make the journey alone.
remembering.heading: We gather
remembering.why_text: Remembering helps us return to God more deeply and more often. As we return, we become more open to the joy, love, compassion, peace, awe, and wonder that make life truly come alive.
remembering.intro1: Homeward began because many people longed for more—more presence, more meaning, and a community where love for God, a connection to the life and teachings of Jesus, and honest questions could live together.
remembering.intro2: We come together to help one another remember what matters most.
remembering.footer_text: Maybe you have been looking for your people, too.

faq.heading: You do not have to know before you come.

items.question: What do you mean by “rooted in Jesus”?
items.answer: We return continually to the life and teachings of Jesus as inspiration for our shared journey. That does not mean everyone has or needs to have the same beliefs. Questions are welcomed, belonging is not conditioned on certainty, and no one is asked to pretend.

items.question: What if I am unsure what I believe?
items.answer: Wherever you are in your understanding of God, you are welcome to begin honestly. Homeward makes room for faith, questions, doubt, hope, and change.

items.question: What are Christian meditation and contemplative prayer?
items.answer: They are time-tested ways of becoming quiet, attentive, and open to God. Practices may use the breath, a prayer word, Scripture, reflection, or silent presence. No prior experience is needed.

items.question: Do you draw from traditions outside Christianity?
items.answer: Homeward is rooted in Jesus and draws primarily from the historic Christian contemplative tradition. Practices such as silence, attention, compassion, gratitude, and awareness of the breath also appear in other spiritual traditions, including Buddhism. We acknowledge those points of connection honestly and respectfully while teaching our practices within a Jesus-centered Christian framework. Homeward is not an attempt to blend religions together. It is a community seeking to follow Jesus deeply while remaining open to truth, wisdom, and love wherever they may be recognized.

items.question: Is Homeward a church?
items.answer: Homeward is forming as a spiritual community rooted in Jesus, beginning with Circles. You do not need to leave an existing church, and you do not need previous church involvement to participate.

items.question: Do I have to schedule a conversation?
items.answer: No. You can take the Journey Reflection, try a practice, explore how Circles work, or simply tell us you are interested. A conversation is available whenever you feel ready.

items.title: Light of Christ
items.description: A guided meditation in which we receive the loving light of Christ, rest in that presence, and allow the light to radiate toward those we love, the wider world, and all creation.

items.title: Breath Prayer
items.description: A simple prayer joined to the natural rhythm of breathing—such as, “Breathing in, I receive peace. Breathing out, I offer love.”

items.title: Maranatha Prayer
items.description: Silently repeating Maranatha—Come, Lord Jesus as a way of gathering the mind, releasing distraction, and welcoming the presence of God.

items.title: Inspired Reading
items.description: A time-honored method and practice for reading Scripture and listening for the words, images, or invitations that speak to your life.

items.title: Daily Reflection
items.subtitle: Noticing God in your day
items.description: A five-step process for reviewing your day with gratitude and honesty, noticing where you felt alive, distant, loved, or invited to grow.

items.title: Prayer of Gratitude
items.description: A gentle practice of remembering the gifts, people, and moments that have sustained us—and allowing gratitude to widen our awareness of God’s goodness.

practices.heading: Simple practices for everyday life.
practices.intro: Homeward practices are simple ways of slowing down, paying attention, and opening our lives to God. No prior experience is needed, and there is nothing to perform or master.
practices.more_text: And more—including Inspired Reading, Daily Reflection, and Prayer of Gratitude.
